system:
You are an expert in OpenSCAD and in designing 3D-printable (FDM) parts for biology laboratories.
Write one complete, self-contained OpenSCAD file that builds exactly the part the user describes.

Rules:
1. Units are millimetres. Use the user's dimensions exactly - they were measured with calipers.
2. Put every dimension in a named variable at the top of the file, with a short comment.
3. Model the part in the print orientation the user gives: it rests on the XY plane at z = 0 and builds upward (+Z). Unless told otherwise, centre it on the origin in X and Y.
4. Use only built-in OpenSCAD: cube, cylinder, sphere, polygon, circle, square, linear_extrude, rotate_extrude, translate, rotate, mirror, union, difference, intersection, hull, for. Do not use include, use or any external library.
5. In difference(), make every cutting shape extend 0.01-1 mm past the faces it cuts, so no faces are exactly coplanar.
6. Set $fn = 64 (or more) on curved shapes so holes come out round and to size.
7. Build repeated features (hole grids, slots, teeth, grooves) with for loops.
8. The file must render to a valid solid with no errors.

Reply with only the code, in a single ```openscad code block.

tasks.user: Design a bench rack for 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes. It is a solid rectangular block 106 mm long (X), 72 mm wide (Y) and 30 mm tall (Z). It has 24 vertical holes in 4 rows (along Y) of 6 holes (along X), 16 mm centre-to-centre in both directions, with the hole grid centred on the block. Each hole is 11.2 mm in diameter and 25 mm deep, open at the top and closed at the bottom, leaving a 5 mm solid floor.

Design a rack for six 50 mL conical (Falcon-type) tubes. It is printed upside down and flipped over after printing. In print orientation: a flat plate 130 mm (X) by 90 mm (Y) and 4 mm thick lies on the bed (z = 0 to 4). The plate has six through-holes, 30.5 mm in diameter, in 2 rows (along Y) of 3 (along X), 40 mm centre-to-centre in both directions, centred on the plate. Two solid walls run along the two long edges of the plate: each wall is 130 mm long (X) and 4 mm thick (Y), flush with the plate's long edge, and rises from the plate to z = 70. The two short ends stay open. After flipping, the rack stands on the two walls and the tubes pass through the holes.

Design a drying rack that holds 10 microscope slides (75 x 25 x 1 mm) standing upright on their long edge. It is a solid base block 90 mm long (X), 45 mm wide (Y) and 20 mm tall (Z). Cut 10 parallel slots into the top face: each slot runs along X, is 77 mm long, 1.6 mm wide (Y) and 10 mm deep, open at the top. The slots are 3.5 mm apart centre-to-centre (in Y), and the group of slots is centred on the block in X and Y.

Design a rack for 96 PCR tubes (0.2 mL) with the standard microplate (ANSI/SLAS) footprint: a block 127.76 mm long (X), 85.48 mm wide (Y) and 20 mm tall (Z). It has 96 vertical through-holes, 6.2 mm in diameter, in 8 rows (along Y) by 12 columns (along X) at 9.0 mm centre-to-centre spacing. The centre of the first hole (A1) is 14.38 mm from the left edge and 11.24 mm from the back edge, so the grid is centred on the block. Cut a 45-degree chamfer with 5 mm legs off the vertical edge at the A1 corner as an orientation mark.

Design a 10-well comb for casting agarose gels, printed lying flat. The whole comb is a flat plate 1.5 mm thick (Z) lying on the bed. Seen from above, it has a straight spine (back bar) 70 mm long (X) and 12 mm wide (Y), and 10 rectangular teeth that hang from one long edge of the spine in the -Y direction. Each tooth is 5.0 mm wide (X) and 12 mm long (Y). The gaps between neighbouring teeth are 1.5 mm, and the row of teeth is centred on the spine in X.

Design a pestle for grinding tissue inside a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, printed standing upright. From bottom to top: (1) a cylindrical handle 8 mm in diameter from z = 0 to z = 45; (2) a cone that tapers from 8 mm diameter at z = 45 to 3 mm diameter at z = 62; (3) a rounded tip: a 3 mm diameter sphere centred at z = 62. For grip, cut four circumferential grooves into the handle, each 2 mm wide (in Z) and 1 mm deep, centred at z = 10, 15, 20 and 25.

Design a small lab funnel, printed upright with the wide opening at the top. A straight spout (tube) with 10 mm outer diameter runs from z = 0 to z = 20. On top of it, a cone widens from 10 mm outer diameter at z = 20 to 60 mm outer diameter at the rim at z = 50. The wall is 1.6 mm thick everywhere (so the spout's bore is 6.8 mm), and the funnel is open at the top and at the bottom so liquid runs straight through.

Design a sowing template that sits inside a 90 mm Petri dish: a flat disc 85 mm in diameter and 2 mm thick, lying on the bed. It has a 7 x 7 grid of 3 mm diameter through-holes with 9 mm centre-to-centre spacing, centred on the disc. Cut a rectangular orientation notch into the rim on the +Y side, centred on the Y axis: 10 mm wide (X) and 4 mm deep (Y, measured in from the rim).

Design a replacement knob for a hotplate stirrer with a 6 mm D-shaft. The knob is a cylinder 30 mm in diameter and 15 mm tall. It is printed with the side that faces the hotplate down on the bed (z = 0). From that bottom face, a D-shaped blind bore goes 12 mm up into the knob: a 6.2 mm diameter circle with one side cut flat, so the distance from the flat to the opposite side of the circle is 4.7 mm. Around the outside, cut 18 evenly spaced vertical grip grooves along the full height; each groove is a 2 mm diameter half-cylinder centred on the outer surface. On the top face, cut a pointer groove 1.5 mm wide and 1 mm deep that runs from the centre to the outer edge, on the same side as the flat of the D.

Design an adapter sleeve that lets a 0.2 mL PCR tube sit in a rack hole made for 1.5 mL tubes. Print it upside down: a collar 13 mm in diameter and 1.5 mm thick lies on the bed (z = 0 to 1.5), and the sleeve body, 10.8 mm in outer diameter, rises from the collar to z = 21.5. A straight 6.2 mm diameter bore runs through the full height, open at both ends.

Design a straight hose-barb reducer that joins silicone tubing with 8 mm inner diameter to tubing with 5 mm inner diameter. Print it standing upright along Z. It is round (rotationally symmetric about the Z axis) and a 3 mm bore runs straight through its full length. From z = 0 to z = 20: two identical barbs for the 8 mm tubing, stacked; each barb is 10 mm tall and its outer diameter grows linearly from 7.5 mm at its bottom to 9.5 mm at its top, then steps straight back to 7.5 mm (a sawtooth profile). From z = 20 to z = 25: a cylindrical collar of 12 mm diameter. From z = 25 to z = 41: two identical barbs for the 5 mm tubing, stacked; each barb is 8 mm tall and its outer diameter shrinks linearly from 6.5 mm at its bottom to 5.0 mm at its top, then steps straight back out to 6.5 mm.

Design a snap-on clip that holds a piece of tubing next to a 12.7 mm (1/2 inch) lab stand rod. It is printed flat: a 10 mm tall extrusion (Z) of a 2-D profile in the XY plane. The profile consists of: (1) a rod ring with 12.7 mm inner diameter and 3 mm wall (18.7 mm outer diameter), centred at the origin, with a 10 mm wide opening cut out of its -X side (everything with x < 0 and -5 < y < 5 is removed from this ring) so it snaps onto the rod; (2) a tubing ring with 6 mm inner diameter and 2 mm wall, centred at x = 15, y = 0, with a 4.5 mm wide opening cut out of its +X side (x > 15 and -2.25 < y < 2.25); (3) a solid bridge 6 mm wide (Y) between x = 8 and x = 12 that joins the two rings without blocking either ring's hole.

Design the housing for a DIY magnetic stirrer built from an 80 mm PC case fan. In use it is an upside-down open box that covers the fan, and its closed top is the stirring surface. Model it in print orientation, i.e. upside down: the 2 mm thick top plate lies on the bed (z = 0 to 2) and four walls, 2.5 mm thick, rise from it to z = 40, where the box is open. The outer size is 90 x 90 mm (X x Y). Drill four 4.5 mm holes for M4 screws through the top plate on a 71.5 mm square pattern centred on the plate (the fan's mounting holes). In one wall, cut a notch for the power cable: 12 mm wide, centred along the wall, reaching 8 mm down from the open edge (from z = 32 to z = 40).

Design an L-shaped mounting bracket for a NEMA 17 stepper motor, e.g. for a syringe pump. Print orientation: the base plate lies on the bed. Base plate: x from -25 to 25, y from 0 to 45, z from 0 to 5, with two 4.5 mm vertical through-holes (M4) at (x = -17, y = 30) and (x = 17, y = 30). Vertical motor plate: x from -25 to 25, y from 0 to 5, z from 0 to 50, standing on the back edge of the base. Through the motor plate (along Y) cut a 23 mm hole for the motor's centring boss with its centre at x = 0, z = 28, and four 3.4 mm holes for M3 screws on a 31 mm square pattern centred on the boss hole. Add two triangular gussets, 5 mm thick, flush with the left and right edges (x = -25 to -20 and x = 20 to 25): each is a right triangle in the YZ plane with legs 20 mm along +Y and 20 mm along +Z, its right-angle corner at y = 5, z = 5 (where the plates meet).

Design a two-part enclosure for a small electronics board (for example an Arduino-based temperature logger). Put both parts in the same file, side by side on the bed with a 10 mm gap between them, so they print together. Part 1, the box: outer size 70 x 50 x 30 mm (X x Y x Z), 2 mm walls, 2 mm floor, open top. Part 2, the lid, printed upside down: a plate 70 x 50 x 2 mm lying on the bed, with a rectangular lip on top of it - a 1.5 mm thick wall, 4 mm tall, whose outer size is 65.6 x 45.6 mm, centred on the plate, so it slides into the box opening with 0.2 mm clearance on each side. Place the lid on the +X side of the box.

Design the buffer tank for a mini horizontal gel-electrophoresis box. It is an open-top rectangular tank with outer dimensions 120 mm (X) x 70 mm (Y) x 40 mm (Z), 3 mm walls and a 3 mm floor. In the middle of the tank, a solid raised platform for the gel tray spans the full inner width (Y) of the tank, is 60 mm long in X (centred), and its top is 10 mm above the inner floor (at z = 13). The platform divides the bottom of the tank into two buffer chambers, one at each end, that connect above the platform. Through each end wall (the walls at the two X ends), drill a 2 mm diameter horizontal hole along X at y = 0, z = 30 for the electrode wires.
